A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OMNI-EPIC and provide readable main texts, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained task descriptions, code, prompts, and settings can be matched across renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original task-generation and reinforcement-learning experiments, including a 200-iteration generation run and a learning run reporting 16 successes, 6 failures, and 1 uninteresting task.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by four additional learning runs and quantitative comparisons against two controls in Section 6 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The archive, task and environment generators, interestingness filtering, specialist-agent training, and success detection remain unchanged. Calling the filter the post-generation model of interestingness clarifies an existing component; the corresponding prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate task generation and R2D2 learning in PyBullet using the same three seed tasks and broad navigation/object-interaction coverage. The additional runs generate further instances within this retained setting.

E2.justification: V1 has no evaluated comparison controls. V2 introduces OMNI-EPIC w/o archive and OMNI-EPIC learning progress only, comparing both against the full method in the diversity and learning-progress experiments.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds controlled evaluations using cell coverage after two-dimensional PCA and progress measured by ANNECS and ANNECS-OMNI. These are new protocols; the original t-SNE visualization and reported DreamerV3 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New ablations test the contributions of archive conditioning and interestingness guidance. The latter control removes both interestingness requests from task-generation prompts and post-generation filtering. Figures 4, 33, and 34 supply evidence absent from v1.

E5.justification: V2 expands the reported learning experiments from one run to five and reports three simulated-learning runs per method for the diversity comparison. It adds median curves, 95% confidence intervals, and Mann-Whitney U tests reporting p < 0.05; v1 lacks this statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The original 16-success, 6-failure, 1-uninteresting-task result is retained. V2 adds four runs and quantitative control comparisons: Figure 4 shows median ANNECS-OMNI reaching 10 for the full method versus 4 for each control at plotted learned-archive size 13. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 6 introduces a limited new metric definition: ANNECS-OMNI adds an interestingness condition to ANNECS's accumulated count of qualifying solved environments. No theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee accompanies this definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about generating diverse, learnable tasks through code. However, the introduction removes the explicit 'under the reward hypothesis' qualification from the claim of creating any simulatable task, making that claim less explicitly conditional.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the ablations as evidence that both the archive and interestingness guidance contribute to diversity, and the ANNECS-OMNI curves as evidence of continued innovation during the measured runs. Existing limitations concerning simulator constraints, specialist agents, and VLM success detection remain.

D1.justification: The new evaluation describes the control's prompt/filter modifications and the embedding-to-PCA-to-bin processing procedure. Existing generated-code listings, prompts, model identifiers, training hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures are retained in the renumbered appendices.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Mackiewicz and Ratajczak (1993), Mouret and Clune (2015), and Pugh et al. (2016) for PCA and diversity measurement. Section 6 also positions ANNECS-OMNI as an extension of ANNECS informed by OMNI; the main related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized method rewrites distinguish task-generation interestingness from post-generation checking. V2 adds a quantitative-results section and two appendices, changes citations to author-year style, and makes small wording edits, while retaining most existing prose and appendix listings.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 4 and Figures 29–34, introducing quantitative plots and four additional task-outcome image grids. It also relabels Figure 1, relocates Figure 3, and changes document styling. Existing figures and both hyperparameter tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V1 relies primarily on qualitative generation examples and one learning run. V2 addresses an important evidential gap through component ablations, additional learning runs, and quantitative comparisons with uncertainty reporting. Small samples and model-judged interestingness still limit the conclusions, and removing the reward-hypothesis caveat slightly reduces precision, but the new controlled evidence substantially strengthens support for the paper's central design.
